purpose: What the ds-web TypeScript layer decisions answered for one assembler-shaped document (expected_ts), and what ds-command-kernel::layer_state answers (expected). Cases naming a divergence were decided for the kernel; see `divergences`.

divergences.D1: An unrecorded companion follows its family's remembered choice, then its authored visibility. The TypeScript read any unrecorded id as visible (`vis[id] !== false`), so a hidden family with an authored-hidden label still reported "some visible" and a parent toggle wrote the wrong value.
divergences.D2: Toggling one unrecorded layer flips its effective visibility. The TypeScript flipped the raw entry (`!vis[id]`), so an unrecorded visible layer "toggled" to visible.
divergences.D3: The kernel records a mounted primary's preference even when the renderer's addLayer throws; the TypeScript dropped it. A renderer failure does not change what the user chose.
